at male.explanation: "At male" means "to paint": Han maler væggen hvid (He paints the wall white). It also works for pictures: Hun maler et billede (She paints a picture). For drawing with a pencil, use at tegne (to draw).

sentence.da: Vi vil **male** væggen hvid.
sentence.en: We want to paint the wall white.

at mangle.explanation: "At mangle" means "to lack" or "to be missing". What is missing comes after it: Jeg mangler en pen (I am missing a pen). Der mangler en stol (A chair is missing).

sentence.da: Vi vil **mangle** en stol til gæsterne.
sentence.en: We will be missing a chair for the guests.

at meditere.explanation: "At meditere" means "to meditate", to sit quietly and calm your mind. Jeg mediterer hver dag means "I meditate every day".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **meditere** hver dag.
sentence.en: I want to meditate every day.

at melde afbud.explanation: "At melde afbud" means "to cancel", when you tell people you cannot come: Han meldte afbud til festen (He told them he could not come to the party). To cancel the event itself, use at aflyse (to cancel).

sentence.da: Jeg må desværre **melde afbud** til mødet.
sentence.en: Unfortunately, I have to tell them I cannot come to the meeting.

at melde sig.explanation: "At melde sig" means "to sign up", and also "to volunteer": Jeg meldte mig til kurset (I signed up for the course). Hvem vil melde sig? (Who will volunteer?)

sentence.da: Hun vil **melde sig** til et kursus.
sentence.en: She wants to sign up for a course.

at melde sig syg.explanation: "At melde sig syg" means "to call in sick", that is, to tell your work or school that you are ill and cannot come. It is about the act of reporting, not the illness itself: Jeg er syg (I am sick) just says how you feel.

sentence.da: Han har feber og må **melde sig syg**.
sentence.en: He has a fever and has to call in sick.

at melde sig til.explanation: "At melde sig til" means "to sign up for" a course, a team or an event: Jeg melder mig til kurset (I sign up for the course). The small word after melder changes with the person: Hun melder sig til (She signs up), Vi melder os til (We sign up).

sentence.da: Hun vil **melde sig til** kurset i næste uge.
sentence.en: She wants to sign up for the course next week.

at melde til politiet.explanation: "At melde til politiet" means "to report to the police". Use it when you tell the police about a crime or an accident: Han meldte det til politiet (He reported it to the police).

forms.en: I have reported to the police

sentence.da: Min nabo vil **melde til politiet**, at cyklen er stjålet.
sentence.en: My neighbor wants to report to the police that the bike was stolen.

at mene.explanation: "At mene" means "to mean / think": you hold an opinion. Jeg mener, at du har ret means "I believe you are right". Hvad mener du? means "What do you mean?". At synes (to think) is for feelings and taste: Jeg synes, at maden er god (I think the food is good). For the meaning of a word, Danish uses at betyde (to mean).

sentence.da: Du må gerne **mene** noget andet.
sentence.en: You are welcome to think something else.

at minde om.explanation: "At minde om" means "to remind of", and also "to resemble": Du minder mig om min bror (You remind me of my brother). To remind someone to do something, add at (to): Jeg minder dig om at ringe (I remind you to call).

sentence.da: Den sang kan **minde om** sommeren.
sentence.en: That song can be reminiscent of summer.

at misforstå.explanation: "At misforstå" means "to misunderstand": Jeg misforstod dig (I misunderstood you). It is built from mis- (wrongly) and at forstå (to understand).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **misforstå** mig, jeg er ikke vred.
sentence.en: Don't misunderstand me, I'm not angry.

at misse.explanation: "At misse" means "to miss", when you are too late for something: Vi missede toget (We missed the train). Missing a person is at savne (to miss): Jeg savner dig (I miss you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **misse** bussen i morgen tidlig.
sentence.en: I don't want to miss the bus tomorrow morning.

at miste.explanation: "At miste" means "to lose" something you had: Jeg mistede min nøgle (I lost my key). It also fits people: Hun mistede sin bedstefar (She lost her grandfather). To lose a game is at tabe: Vi tabte kampen (We lost the match).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **miste** min telefon igen.
sentence.en: I don't want to lose my phone again.

at mjave.explanation: "At mjave" means "to meow", the sound a cat makes: Katten mjaver, fordi den er sulten (The cat meows because it is hungry). Purring is at spinde: Katten spinder (The cat purrs).

sentence.da: Jeg kan høre katten **mjave** udenfor.
sentence.en: I can hear the cat meow outside.

at modtage.explanation: "At modtage" means "to receive": Jeg har modtaget din mail (I have received your email). It sounds a bit formal. In everyday speech, Danes often say at få (to get): Jeg fik en gave (I got a gift).

sentence.da: Vi skal **modtage** en pakke i morgen.
sentence.en: We are going to receive a package tomorrow.

at more sig.explanation: "At more sig" means "to have fun", and sig changes with the person: Vi morer os (We are having fun). Du morer dig (You are having fun).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **more sig** til festen.
sentence.en: The children are going to have fun at the party.

at motionere.explanation: "At motionere" means "to exercise" to stay healthy, for example by walking or swimming: Jeg motionerer tre gange om ugen (I exercise three times a week). The thing itself is motion (exercise): Motion er sundt (Exercise is healthy).

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at jeg skal **motionere** mere.
sentence.en: The doctor says that I should exercise more.

at måle.explanation: "At måle" means "to measure", finding out the size or amount of something: Jeg måler bordet (I am measuring the table). It works for temperature too: Lægen måler min temperatur (The doctor is taking my temperature).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **måle** vinduet og købe nye gardiner.
sentence.en: I need to measure the window and buy new curtains.

at måtte.explanation: "At måtte" means "may / must": it covers being allowed to and having to. Må jeg gå? means "May I go?", while Jeg må gå nu means "I have to go now". Du må ikke means "You must not", a strong warning. Another action word follows straight after it, with no at.

forms.en: I was allowed to / had to

sentence.da: Vi kommer til at **måtte** vente en time.
sentence.en: We will have to wait an hour.

at mærke.explanation: "At mærke" means "to feel" something physical, and also "to notice": Jeg mærker regnen (I feel the rain). Han mærkede ikke noget (He did not notice anything).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **mærke** vinden i mit ansigt.
sentence.en: I can feel the wind on my face.

at møde op.explanation: "At møde op" means "to show up", to come where you are expected: Han mødte op til tiden (He showed up on time). It is often said about people who do not: Hun mødte ikke op (She did not show up).

sentence.da: Alle skal **møde op** klokken otte.
sentence.en: Everyone has to show up at eight o'clock.

at mødes.explanation: "At mødes" means "to meet each other", usually by plan: Vi mødes i morgen (We meet tomorrow). Without the s, at møde means "to meet" someone: Jeg møder Anna (I meet Anna).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **mødes** på cafeen i morgen.
sentence.en: We would like to meet at the cafe tomorrow.

en madkasse.explanation: "En madkasse" means "a lunch box", the box you bring food in to school or work: Jeg har min madkasse med på arbejde (I have my lunch box with me at work).

sentence.da: Min søn tager sin **madkasse** med i skole.
sentence.en: My son takes his lunch box to school.

en madpakke.explanation: "En madpakke" means "a packed lunch", usually sandwiches you make at home and take to school or work: Har du madpakke med? (Do you have a packed lunch with you?)

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **madpakke** med på arbejde.
sentence.en: I take my packed lunch to work.

en madras.explanation: "En madras" means "a mattress", the part of a bed you lie on: Madrassen er hård (The mattress is hard).

sentence.da: Jeg sover bedre på en blød **madras**.
sentence.en: I sleep better on a soft mattress.

en mafia.explanation: "En mafia" means "a mafia", an organized criminal group: Mafiaen kontrollerer byen (The mafia controls the city). The word is used for the Italian Mafia and for similar groups.

sentence.da: Filmen handler om en **mafia** i New York.
sentence.en: The movie is about a mafia in New York.

en mail.explanation: "En mail" means "an email". It is the short everyday word for en e-mail (an email): Jeg sender en mail means "I am sending an email".

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig en **mail** i dag.
sentence.en: I am sending you an email today.

en maler.explanation: "En maler" means "a painter", both an artist and someone who paints walls: En maler maler vores køkken (A painter is painting our kitchen). The situation shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: Min bror er **maler** og maler huse.
sentence.en: My brother is a painter and paints houses.

en mand.explanation: "En mand" means "a man" or "a husband". With min (my) it means husband: min mand is my husband.

sentence.da: Min **mand** og jeg har to børn.
sentence.en: My husband and I have two children.

en mandel.explanation: "En mandel" means "an almond": Kagen er lavet med mandler (The cake is made with almonds). It also means a tonsil: Han fik fjernet mandlerne (He had his tonsils removed).

sentence.da: Marcipan er lavet af **mandel** og sukker.
sentence.en: Marzipan is made of almond and sugar.

en mango.explanation: "En mango" means "a mango", a sweet fruit with a big pit. You can eat it fresh or blend it: Jeg laver en smoothie med mango (I make a smoothie with mango).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en **mango** i små stykker.
sentence.en: I cut a mango into small pieces.

en mappe.explanation: "En mappe" means "a folder", on a computer or for papers. Files go inside it: En fil ligger i en mappe (A file is in a folder).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger alle billederne i en ny **mappe**.
sentence.en: I put all the pictures in a new folder.

en mark.explanation: "En mark" means "a field", farmland where crops grow: Der vokser korn på marken (Grain grows in the field). Vi går en tur over marken (We walk across the field).

sentence.da: Bonden kører en traktor ud på sin **mark**.
sentence.en: The farmer drives a tractor out onto his field.

en markedsbod.explanation: "En markedsbod" means "a market stall", a small booth where a seller shows goods at a market: Markedsboden åbner klokken otte (The market stall opens at eight).

sentence.da: Jeg køber friske æbler i en **markedsbod**.
sentence.en: I buy fresh apples at a market stall.

en mascara.explanation: "En mascara" means "a mascara", makeup that darkens your eyelashes. You often drop en when you use it: Jeg tager mascara på (I put on mascara).

sentence.da: Jeg tager altid **mascara** på, når jeg skal ud.
sentence.en: I always put on mascara when I go out.

en maske.explanation: "En maske" means "a mask", something you wear over your face: Hun har en maske på (She has a mask on). To put one on, say at tage en maske på (to put on a mask).

sentence.da: Pigen tager en **maske** på til festen.
sentence.en: The girl puts on a mask for the party.

en maskine.explanation: "En maskine" means "a machine", a device with moving parts that does work for you: Maskinen larmer meget (The machine makes a lot of noise). It is the last part of words like en vaskemaskine (a washing machine).

sentence.da: Den nye **maskine** er hurtig, men larmer meget.
sentence.en: The new machine is fast but makes a lot of noise.

en masse.explanation: "En masse" means "a lot": en masse penge (a lot of money). Unlike English, it has no af (of) in between. Jeg har en masse arbejde (I have a lot of work).

sentence.da: Der var en **masse** mennesker i byen.
sentence.en: There were a lot of people in town.

en mave.explanation: "En mave" means "a stomach" or "a belly". Jeg har ondt i maven means "My stomach hurts", and Han har en stor mave means "He has a big belly".

sentence.da: Min **mave** gør ondt i dag.
sentence.en: My stomach hurts today.

en mavepine.explanation: "En mavepine" means "a stomachache", built from mave (stomach) and pine (pain). You say Jeg har mavepine (I have a stomachache) without en. Jeg har ondt i maven (I have a pain in the stomach) means nearly the same.

sentence.da: Jeg har **mavepine** og vil ikke spise.
sentence.en: I have a stomachache and don't want to eat.

en medalje.explanation: "En medalje" means "a medal", a prize for winning: Hun fik en medalje efter løbet (She got a medal after the race). Second place gets a sølvmedalje (silver medal).

sentence.da: Min datter vandt en **medalje** i svømning.
sentence.en: My daughter won a medal in swimming.

en medarbejder.explanation: "En medarbejder" means "an employee", a person who works for a company: Vi har ti medarbejdere (We have ten employees). It is built from med (with) and arbejder (worker), so it means someone who works with you.

sentence.da: Vores nye **medarbejder** starter på mandag.
sentence.en: Our new employee starts on Monday.

en medisterpølse.explanation: "En medisterpølse" means "a Danish pork sausage", a thick sausage of minced pork and spices that is usually fried: Jeg steger en medisterpølse (I am frying a medister sausage).

sentence.da: Til aftensmad steger vi en **medisterpølse** med kartofler.
sentence.en: For dinner we fry a medister sausage with potatoes.

en mellemlanding.explanation: "En mellemlanding" means "a layover", a stop at another airport on the way to the final place: Flyet har en mellemlanding i London (The flight has a layover in London). It is built from mellem (between) and landing (landing).

sentence.da: På turen til Thailand har vi en **mellemlanding** i Dubai.
sentence.en: On the trip to Thailand, we have a layover in Dubai.

en melodi.explanation: "En melodi" means "a melody", the tune of a song: Jeg kan godt lide melodien (I like the melody). To hum it, say at nynne (to hum): Han nynner en melodi (He hums a tune).

sentence.da: Jeg kender den smukke **melodi**, men ikke teksten.
sentence.en: I know the beautiful melody, but not the lyrics.

en melon.explanation: "En melon" means "a melon". Other kinds add a word in front, like en honningmelon (a honeydew melon).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en sød **melon** hjemme.
sentence.en: I eat a sweet melon at home.

en mening.explanation: "En mening" means "an opinion": Hvad er din mening? (What is your opinion?). It also means "sense": Det giver ingen mening (That makes no sense).

sentence.da: Jeg har en anden **mening** end dig.
sentence.en: I have a different opinion than you.

en menu.explanation: "En menu" means "a menu", the list of food at a restaurant. You can ask Kan jeg få menuen? (Can I have the menu?). Dagens menu means "the menu of the day".

sentence.da: Vi får en **menu** og vælger mad.
sentence.en: We get a menu and choose food.

en mester.explanation: "En mester" means "a champion" and also "a master": Holdet blev mester i år (The team became champion this year). A trained craftsman is also mester: en tømrermester (a master carpenter).

sentence.da: Min bror er **mester** i skak.
sentence.en: My brother is a chess champion.

en meter.explanation: "En meter" means "a meter". It does not change after a number: to meter means "two meters", and "to meter høj" means "two meters tall".

sentence.da: Han er over to **meter** høj.
sentence.en: He is over two meters tall.

en metro.explanation: "En metro" means "a metro", the underground train. You travel med metroen (by metro). Do not mix it up with S-tog (the S-train), which is a different train line.

sentence.da: Jeg kører med **metro** under jorden.
sentence.en: I ride the metro underground.

en middag.explanation: "En middag" means "a dinner", the main hot meal, eaten in the evening. It can also mean "noon", but the meal in the middle of the day is frokost (lunch).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **middag** klokken seks om aftenen.
sentence.en: We eat dinner at six in the evening.

en midtergang.explanation: "En midtergang" means "an aisle", the walkway between rows of seats on a plane, bus or train: Jeg sidder ved midtergangen (I sit by the aisle). Kan jeg få en plads ved midtergangen? (Can I get a seat by the aisle?)

sentence.da: Han går ned ad en lang **midtergang** i flyet.
sentence.en: He walks down a long aisle in the plane.

en mikrobølgeovn.explanation: "En mikrobølgeovn" means "a microwave oven", used to heat up food fast. People often shorten it to en mikro (a microwave): Jeg varmer maden i mikroen (I heat the food in the microwave).

sentence.da: Vi har en ny **mikrobølgeovn** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We have a new microwave oven in the kitchen.

en mikrofon.explanation: "En mikrofon" means "a microphone". On a call you may hear: Din mikrofon er slået fra (Your microphone is off). Slå din mikrofon til (Turn on your microphone).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke høre dig, fordi din **mikrofon** er slukket.
sentence.en: I cannot hear you because your microphone is off.

en mikroovn.explanation: "En mikroovn" means "a microwave". The longer name is en mikrobølgeovn (a microwave oven), but mikroovn is shorter: Jeg varmer maden i mikroovnen (I heat the food in the microwave).

sentence.da: Jeg varmer suppen i min **mikroovn**.
sentence.en: I heat the soup in my microwave.

en milkshake.explanation: "En milkshake" means "a milkshake", a cold drink of milk and ice cream. To order one, say: Jeg vil gerne have en milkshake (I would like a milkshake).

sentence.da: Børnene vil have en **milkshake** med chokolade.
sentence.en: The children want a milkshake with chocolate.

en milliard.explanation: "En milliard" means "a billion" (a thousand million). Careful with the Danish word en billion: it means a trillion (a million million), not a billion.

sentence.da: Kina har over en **milliard** mennesker.
sentence.en: China has over a billion people.

en minister.explanation: "En minister" means "a minister", a member of the government who leads one area: Ministeren holder en tale (The minister is giving a speech). Put the area first to name the job: sundhedsminister (health minister).

sentence.da: Den nye **minister** vil bygge flere skoler.
sentence.en: The new minister wants to build more schools.

en misforståelse.explanation: "En misforståelse" means "a misunderstanding", when two people understood something differently: Det var bare en misforståelse (It was just a misunderstanding). Vi havde en misforståelse (We had a misunderstanding).

sentence.da: Undskyld, det var bare en **misforståelse**.
sentence.en: Sorry, it was just a misunderstanding.

en mobil.explanation: "En mobil" means "a mobile phone", the short everyday word for en mobiltelefon (a mobile phone). En telefon (a phone) can also be a landline.

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig fra min **mobil**.
sentence.en: I call you from my mobile phone.

en mobiltelefon.explanation: "En mobiltelefon" means "a mobile phone", the full word, made from mobil (mobile) and telefon (phone). In daily speech, people usually say en mobil (a mobile phone) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til min mor på min **mobiltelefon**.
sentence.en: I call my mother on my mobile phone.

en model.explanation: "En model" means "a model": a small copy, a type of car or a person who shows clothes. Hvilken model er bilen? (Which model is the car?) En model af et fly (A model of a plane).

sentence.da: Min onkel bygger en **model** af et skib.
sentence.en: My uncle is building a model of a ship.

en moppe.explanation: "En moppe" means "a mop", used to wash a floor with water: Jeg vasker gulvet med en moppe (I wash the floor with a mop). Moppen er våd (The mop is wet).

sentence.da: Gulvet er snavset, så jeg henter en **moppe**.
sentence.en: The floor is dirty, so I get a mop.

en mor.explanation: "En mor" means "a mother". To talk about your own mother, say min mor (my mother). You can also use mor like a name when speaking to her: Hej, mor! (Hi, mom!).

sentence.da: Min **mor** er gift med min far.
sentence.en: My mother is married to my father.

en morbror.explanation: "En morbror" means "an uncle", your mother's brother: Min morbror er læge (My uncle is a doctor). Your father's brother is en farbror (an uncle).

sentence.da: Min **morbror** er min mors bror og bor i Roskilde.
sentence.en: My uncle is my mother's brother and lives in Roskilde.

en morder.explanation: "En morder" means "a murderer", a person who kills someone on purpose: Politiet leder efter morderen (The police are looking for the murderer). It is built from mord (a murder).

sentence.da: Politiet leder efter en **morder**, der er flygtet.
sentence.en: The police are looking for a murderer who has escaped.

en morfar.explanation: "En morfar" means "a grandfather", your mother's father: mor (mother) plus far (father). Your father's father is en farfar (a grandfather, father's father).

sentence.da: Min **morfar** er min mors far.
sentence.en: My grandfather is my mother's father.

en morgen.explanation: "En morgen" means "a morning". Do not mix it up with i morgen (tomorrow) or i morges (this morning). Om morgenen means "in the morning" and "godmorgen" means "good morning".

sentence.da: Hver **morgen** spiser jeg morgenmad og drikker kaffe.
sentence.en: Every morning I eat breakfast and drink coffee.

en morgenkaffe.explanation: "En morgenkaffe" means "a morning coffee", the first cup of the day. It is built from morgen (morning) and kaffe (coffee): Jeg drikker min morgenkaffe i sengen (I drink my morning coffee in bed).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker min **morgenkaffe** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: I drink my morning coffee in the kitchen.

en morgenrutine.explanation: "En morgenrutine" means "a morning routine", the things you do every morning in the same order: Først bruser jeg, så spiser jeg morgenmad (First I shower, then I eat breakfast).

sentence.da: Min **morgenrutine** er kaffe, avis og en kort gåtur.
sentence.en: My morning routine is coffee, newspaper and a short walk.

en mormor.explanation: "En mormor" means "a grandmother", your mother's mother: mor (mother) plus mor (mother) again. Your father's mother is en farmor (a grandmother, father's mother).

sentence.da: Min **mormor** er min mors mor.
sentence.en: My grandmother is my mother's mother.

en moster.explanation: "En moster" means "an aunt", your mother's sister: Vi besøger min moster i weekenden (We are visiting my aunt on the weekend). Your father's sister is en faster (an aunt).

sentence.da: Min **moster** er min mors søster og bor i Odense.
sentence.en: My aunt is my mother's sister and lives in Odense.

en motor.explanation: "En motor" means "an engine". Danish uses one word for both engine and motor: Plæneklipperen har en lille motor (The lawn mower has a small motor). Bilens motor er gået i stå (The car's engine has stalled).

sentence.da: Bådens **motor** larmer meget, når vi sejler.
sentence.en: The boat's engine is very loud when we sail.

en motorcykel.explanation: "En motorcykel" means "a motorcycle". It is built from motor (engine) and cykel (bicycle): Han kører på motorcykel til arbejde (He rides a motorcycle to work).

sentence.da: Min bror kører til arbejde på en stor **motorcykel**.
sentence.en: My brother rides to work on a big motorcycle.

en motorcyklist.explanation: "En motorcyklist" means "a motorcyclist", a person who rides a motorcycle: Motorcyklisten kørte for stærkt (The motorcyclist drove too fast).

sentence.da: En **motorcyklist** skal altid bruge hjelm.
sentence.en: A motorcyclist must always wear a helmet.

en motorvej.explanation: "En motorvej" means "a highway", a big road with several lanes. It is built from motor (engine) and vej (road): Vi kører på motorvejen (We are driving on the highway).

sentence.da: Vi skal køre på **motorvej** i to timer.
sentence.en: We have to drive on the highway for two hours.

en muffin.explanation: "En muffin" means "a muffin", a small, sweet cake baked in a paper cup: Jeg bager muffins til fødselsdagen (I bake muffins for the birthday).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **muffin** med blåbær.
sentence.en: I would like a muffin with blueberries.

en muffinform.explanation: "En muffinform" means "a muffin tin", the pan with small cups for baking muffins: Jeg hælder dejen i muffinformen (I pour the batter into the muffin tin).

sentence.da: Hun hælder dejen i en **muffinform**.
sentence.en: She pours the batter into a muffin tin.

en mulighed.explanation: "En mulighed" means "a possibility", and also "an opportunity" or "an option": Det er en god mulighed (That is a good opportunity). Jeg har to muligheder (I have two options).

sentence.da: Det er den eneste **mulighed**, vi har.
sentence.en: It is the only option we have.

en mund.explanation: "En mund" means "a mouth". Hold munden! means "Shut up!" and is rude. Åbn munden means "Open your mouth".

sentence.da: Jeg spiser og taler med min **mund**.
sentence.en: I eat and talk with my mouth.

en mur.explanation: "En mur" means "a wall" outside, like around a garden or on a house: en høj mur (a tall wall). For a wall inside a room, use en væg (a wall).

sentence.da: Der er en høj **mur** om haven.
sentence.en: There is a tall wall around the garden.

en mursten.explanation: "En mursten" means "a brick". It is mur (wall) plus sten (stone): Huset er bygget af mursten (The house is built of bricks).

sentence.da: Det gamle hus er bygget af røde **mursten**.
sentence.en: The old house is built of red bricks.

en mus.explanation: "En mus" means "a mouse". It also means the computer mouse, en computermus (a computer mouse). The plural looks the same: to mus means "two mice". Do not mix it up with en rotte (a rat).

sentence.da: Katten ser en lille **mus**.
sentence.en: The cat sees a small mouse.

en musiker.explanation: "En musiker" means "a musician", someone who plays an instrument: Musikeren spiller guitar (The musician plays the guitar). It comes from musik (music).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **musiker** og spiller i et band.
sentence.en: My uncle is a musician and plays in a band.

en musikfestival.explanation: "En musikfestival" means "a music festival", a big event with many bands, often outdoors in summer: Vi tager på musikfestival (We are going to a music festival). It is built from musik (music) and festival.

sentence.da: Hver sommer hører vi mange bands på en **musikfestival**.
sentence.en: Every summer we hear many bands at a music festival.

en muskel.explanation: "En muskel" means "a muscle", the body part that lets you move: Jeg træner mine muskler (I work out my muscles). Muskelsmerter (muscle pain) is a common word.

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt i en **muskel** i ryggen.
sentence.en: I have a sore muscle in my back.

en musling.explanation: "En musling" means "a mussel" or "a clam", a small sea animal with two hard shells. Vi spiser muslinger med hvidløg (We eat mussels with garlic).

sentence.da: Hun åbner en **musling** og finder en perle.
sentence.en: She opens a mussel and finds a pearl.

en myg.explanation: "En myg" means "a mosquito", the small insect that bites you in summer: Jeg blev stukket af en myg (I was bitten by a mosquito). A fly that lands on food is en flue (a fly).

sentence.da: En **myg** stak mig i armen i nat.
sentence.en: A mosquito bit me on the arm last night.

en myre.explanation: "En myre" means "an ant", a tiny insect that lives in large groups: Der er myrer i køkkenet (There are ants in the kitchen). Myrerne bærer mad hjem (The ants carry food home).

sentence.da: Der går en **myre** hen over bordet.
sentence.en: An ant walks across the table.

en måde.explanation: "En måde" means "a way" of doing something. På den måde means "in that way", and "på en eller anden måde" means "somehow". Do not mix it up with en vej (a road or path).

sentence.da: Det er en god **måde** at lære på.
sentence.en: That is a good way to learn.

en måge.explanation: "En måge" means "a seagull", a bird you see at the sea and in harbors: Mågerne skriger over havnen (The seagulls cry over the harbor).

sentence.da: En **måge** stjal min is ved havnen.
sentence.en: A seagull stole my ice cream at the harbor.

en målmand.explanation: "En målmand" means "a goalkeeper", the player who stops the ball from going into the goal: Målmanden tog bolden (The goalkeeper caught the ball).

sentence.da: Han vil være **målmand**, fordi han griber bolden godt.
sentence.en: He wants to be a goalkeeper because he catches the ball well.

en måne.explanation: "En måne" means "a moon". Do not mix it up with en måned (a month), which starts the same.

sentence.da: Om natten ser vi en **måne**.
sentence.en: At night we see a moon.

en måned.explanation: "En måned" means "a month". Om måneden means "per month", i denne måned means "this month", and næste måned means "next month".

sentence.da: Der er cirka tredive dage i en **måned**.
sentence.en: There are about thirty days in a month.

en mængde.explanation: "En mængde" means "an amount", how much of something there is: en stor mængde vand (a large amount of water). For things you can count, use et antal (a number): et antal bøger (a number of books).

sentence.da: Vi drikker en stor **mængde** vand.
sentence.en: We drink a large amount of water.

en mølle.explanation: "En mølle" means "a mill", a building or machine that grinds grain: Møllen maler kornet (The mill grinds the grain). A windmill is en vindmølle.

sentence.da: Bageren køber mel fra den gamle **mølle**.
sentence.en: The baker buys flour from the old mill.

en mønt.explanation: "En mønt" means "a coin": Jeg har en mønt i lommen (I have a coin in my pocket). Paper money is en seddel (a banknote).

sentence.da: Jeg fandt en **mønt** på gaden.
sentence.en: I found a coin on the street.

et magasin.explanation: "Et magasin" means "a magazine", with articles and photos: Jeg læser et magasin om mad (I read a magazine about food). In everyday speech, Danes often say et blad (a magazine) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg læser et **magasin** i venteværelset.
sentence.en: I read a magazine in the waiting room.

et maleri.explanation: "Et maleri" means "a painting", a finished picture made with paint: Jeg køber et maleri til stuen (I am buying a painting for the living room). The person who makes it is en maler (a painter).

sentence.da: Der hænger et flot **maleri** over sofaen.
sentence.en: A beautiful painting hangs over the sofa.

et maraton.explanation: "Et maraton" means "a marathon", a long race of about 42 kilometers: Hun løber et maraton i maj (She is running a marathon in May). Danes also say et maratonløb (a marathon race) for the same thing.

sentence.da: Hun træner hårdt til sit første **maraton**.
sentence.en: She is training hard for her first marathon.

et mareridt.explanation: "Et mareridt" means "a nightmare", both a bad dream and a terrible situation: Trafikken var et mareridt (The traffic was a nightmare). Barnet vågnede efter et mareridt (The child woke up after a nightmare).

sentence.da: Jeg havde et forfærdeligt **mareridt** i nat.
sentence.en: I had a terrible nightmare last night.

et marked.explanation: "Et marked" means "a market", such as an open-air place where people sell fruit, vegetables or second-hand things.

sentence.da: Vi køber frugt og grøntsager på et **marked**.
sentence.en: We buy fruit and vegetables at a market.

et materiale.explanation: "Et materiale" means "a material", what something is made of: Træ er et godt materiale (Wood is a good material). It can also mean information or study material: Jeg læser materialet (I read the material).

sentence.da: Stål er et stærkt **materiale**.
sentence.en: Steel is a strong material.

et medicinskab.explanation: "Et medicinskab" means "a medicine cabinet", a small cabinet where you keep pills and bandages: Plasteret ligger i medicinskabet (The Band-Aid is in the medicine cabinet). It is built from medicin (medicine) and skab (cabinet).

sentence.da: Pillerne ligger i et lille **medicinskab** på badeværelset.
sentence.en: The pills are in a small medicine cabinet in the bathroom.

et medlem.explanation: "Et medlem" means "a member" of a group, club or team: Hun er medlem af en klub (She is a member of a club). Add af (of) to say which group.

sentence.da: Min bror er **medlem** af en fodboldklub.
sentence.en: My brother is a member of a soccer club.

et mellemnavn.explanation: "Et mellemnavn" means "a middle name", a name between the first and last name. It is made of mellem (between) and et navn (a name).

sentence.da: Marie er mit **mellemnavn**.
sentence.en: Marie is my middle name.

et menneske.explanation: "Et menneske" means "a human being", as opposed to an animal. Its plural mennesker is the everyday word for "people", as in mange mennesker (many people).

sentence.da: Du er et **menneske**, ikke et dyr.
sentence.en: You are a human being, not an animal.

et menukort.explanation: "Et menukort" means "a menu", the list of dishes and drinks in a restaurant. You can ask a waiter Må jeg se menukortet? (May I see the menu?). En menu is a set meal with several courses.

sentence.da: Vi ser på et **menukort** i restauranten.
sentence.en: We look at a menu in the restaurant.

et metal.explanation: "Et metal" means "a metal": Guld er et metal (Gold is a metal). Metal is also the name of a loud music style: Jeg hører metal (I listen to metal).

sentence.da: Aluminium er et let **metal**.
sentence.en: Aluminum is a light metal.

et minut.explanation: "Et minut" means "a minute". To ask someone to wait, you can say Vent et øjeblik (wait a moment) or Vent et minut (wait a minute).

sentence.da: Et **minut** er tres sekunder.
sentence.en: A minute is sixty seconds.

et missil.explanation: "Et missil" means "a missile", a weapon that flies and explodes: Missilet landede i havet (The missile landed in the sea). A rocket for space or fireworks is en raket (a rocket).

sentence.da: Et **missil** ramte en bygning i nat.
sentence.en: A missile hit a building last night.

et monster.explanation: "Et monster" means "a monster": Filmen handler om et monster (The film is about a monster). Do not mix it up with et mønster (a pattern), which looks almost the same.

sentence.da: Barnet er bange for et **monster** under sengen.
sentence.en: The child is afraid of a monster under the bed.

et monument.explanation: "Et monument" means "a monument", a big structure that honors a person or an event: Der er et monument for kongen (There is a monument for the king).

sentence.da: Det store **monument** minder om krigen.
sentence.en: The big monument is a reminder of the war.

et mord.explanation: "Et mord" means "a murder", when one person kills another on purpose: Politiet undersøger mordet (The police are investigating the murder). Han blev anholdt for mordet (He was arrested for the murder).

sentence.da: Politiet undersøger det **mord**, der skete i går.
sentence.en: The police are investigating the murder that happened yesterday.

et motel.explanation: "Et motel" means "a motel", a simple hotel by the road for people traveling by car: Vi sov på et motel (We slept at a motel).

sentence.da: Vi sover på et **motel** ved motorvejen.
sentence.en: We are sleeping at a motel by the highway.

et museum.explanation: "Et museum" means "a museum", a place with art, history or science to look at. You say på museet for "at the museum".

sentence.da: Vi ser gamle ting på et **museum**.
sentence.en: We see old things at a museum.

et mål.explanation: "Et mål" means "a goal", in life and in sports: Mit mål er at løbe et maraton (My goal is to run a marathon). Han scorede to mål (He scored two goals).

sentence.da: Mit **mål** er at tale godt dansk.
sentence.en: My goal is to speak good Danish.

et målebånd.explanation: "Et målebånd" means "a tape measure". It is built from at måle (to measure) and et bånd (a band): Hvor langt er sofaen? Hent målebåndet! (How long is the sofa? Get the tape measure!)

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **målebånd**, når jeg køber møbler.
sentence.en: I use a tape measure when I buy furniture.

et målebæger.explanation: "Et målebæger" means "a measuring cup", a cup with marks that show how much liquid or flour you pour: Fyld målebægeret med mælk (Fill the measuring cup with milk).

sentence.da: Jeg hælder vand i et **målebæger**.
sentence.en: I pour water into a measuring cup.

et måltid.explanation: "Et måltid" means "a meal", any occasion when you sit down to eat, like breakfast, lunch or dinner. It is the occasion, not the food itself: for "food" Danes say mad.

sentence.da: Dagens vigtigste **måltid** er morgenmad.
sentence.en: The most important meal of the day is breakfast.

et månedskort.explanation: "Et månedskort" means "a monthly pass", a ticket you can use as much as you like for a month: Jeg har et månedskort til metroen (I have a monthly pass for the metro). It is built from måned (month) and kort (card).

sentence.da: Med et **månedskort** kan jeg tage bussen hver dag.
sentence.en: With a monthly pass, I can take the bus every day.

et mærke.explanation: "Et mærke" means "a brand", and also "a mark": Hvilket mærke er din jakke? (What brand is your jacket?). It can be a mark on a surface too: et mærke på væggen (a mark on the wall).

sentence.da: Det er et dyrt **mærke**, men jakken er flot.
sentence.en: It is an expensive brand, but the jacket is nice.

et møbel.explanation: "Et møbel" means "a piece of furniture": Reolen er et møbel (The bookshelf is a piece of furniture). The plural møbler means "furniture" in general: Vi køber nye møbler (We are buying new furniture).

sentence.da: Det er et dyrt **møbel**, men det er flot.
sentence.en: It is an expensive piece of furniture, but it is beautiful.

et møde.explanation: "Et møde" means "a meeting", for example at work. Mødet er i morgen means "The meeting is tomorrow".

sentence.da: Min chef har et **møde** i dag.
sentence.en: My boss has a meeting today.

et mønster.explanation: "Et mønster" means "a pattern", on cloth or in how things repeat: Tæppet har et pænt mønster (The rug has a nice pattern).

sentence.da: Der er et fint **mønster** på kjolen.
sentence.en: There is a nice pattern on the dress.

mad.explanation: "Mad" means "food" in general: Jeg elsker dansk mad (I love Danish food). For one dish, use en ret (a dish). En mad means "a sandwich", so do not mix them up.

sentence.da: Jeg er sulten og vil have **mad**.
sentence.en: I am hungry and want food.

madlavning.explanation: "Madlavning" means "cooking", the activity of making meals: Jeg elsker madlavning (I love cooking). To say someone is cooking right now, use Han laver mad (He is cooking).

sentence.da: Min bror kan godt lide **madlavning**.
sentence.en: My brother likes cooking.

mager.explanation: "Mager" means "lean" for food and "skinny" for people: Kyllingebryst er magert (Chicken breast is lean). For a person, it can sound negative, so tynd (thin) is milder.

sentence.da: Jeg vil have en **mager** bøf.
sentence.en: I want a lean steak.

magisk.explanation: "Magisk" means "magical", like magic in stories: en magisk bog (a magical book). It also describes a wonderful moment: Det var magisk! (It was magical!)

sentence.da: Troldmanden har en **magisk** stav i hånden.
sentence.en: The wizard has a magic wand in his hand.

maj.explanation: "Maj" means "May" and sounds like the English word "my". Month names start with a small letter in Danish, so you write maj in the middle of a sentence: Det er varmt i maj (It is warm in May).

sentence.da: Det er varmt i **maj**.
sentence.en: It is warm in May.

majs.explanation: "Majs" means "corn", the yellow kind you eat as a vegetable. It is used without en: Jeg spiser majs (I eat corn).

sentence.da: Popcorn er lavet af **majs**.
sentence.en: Popcorn is made of corn.

makeup.explanation: "Makeup" means "makeup", the same word as in English. To put it on, say tage makeup på: Hun tager makeup på (She puts on makeup).

sentence.da: Hun bruger aldrig **makeup** i skolen.
sentence.en: She never uses makeup at school.

maling.explanation: "Maling" means "paint": Væggen får ny maling (The wall gets new paint). A picture on a wall is et maleri (a painting), not maling.

sentence.da: Vi skal bruge blå **maling** til soveværelset.
sentence.en: We need blue paint for the bedroom.

man.explanation: "Man" means "you" or "one" for anybody, people in general. Compare Du kan købe billetter (You can buy tickets — said to one person) with Man kan købe billetter her (You can buy tickets here — anyone can). Do not mix it up with en mand (a man).

sentence.da: Her må **man** ikke parkere.
sentence.en: You may not park here.

mandag.explanation: "En mandag" means "a Monday". På mandag means "on Monday" (the coming one), om mandagen means "on Mondays" in general, and "i mandags" means "last Monday". Day names start with a small letter in Danish.

sentence.da: Jeg skal på arbejde på **mandag**.
sentence.en: I have to go to work on Monday.

mandlig.explanation: "Mandlig" means "male" and is built on mand (man). It is used for people and animals: en mandlig kollega (a male colleague).

sentence.da: Han er en **mandlig** sygeplejerske.
sentence.en: He is a male nurse.

mange.explanation: "Mange" means "many" for things you can count: mange biler (many cars). For things you cannot count, like water, use meget (a lot, much): meget vand (a lot of water).

sentence.da: Jeg har **mange** venner.
sentence.en: I have many friends.

mange tak.explanation: "Mange tak" means "many thanks", a bit stronger than plain tak (thanks). Add for and what you are thankful for: Mange tak for hjælpen (Thank you very much for the help). The reply is selv tak (you're welcome) or ingen årsag (no problem).

forms.en: Thank you very much for the help.

sentence.da: Her er din kaffe. – **Mange tak**!
sentence.en: Here is your coffee. – Thank you very much!

marcipan.explanation: "Marcipan" means "marzipan", a sweet paste of almonds and sugar: Kransekagen er lavet af marcipan (The ring cake is made of marzipan). Jeg kan godt lide marcipan (I like marzipan).

sentence.da: Kagen er fyldt med **marcipan** og mandler.
sentence.en: The cake is filled with marzipan and almonds.

marmelade.explanation: "Marmelade" means "jam" or "marmalade", a sweet fruit spread for bread: Jeg smører marmelade på brødet (I spread jam on the bread). Jeg kan godt lide marmelade (I like jam).

sentence.da: Hun spiser brød med smør og **marmelade**.
sentence.en: She eats bread with butter and jam.

marts.explanation: "Marts" means "March". Month names start with a small letter in Danish. Dates are said like den tiende marts (the tenth of March).

sentence.da: Det er koldt i **marts**.
sentence.en: It is cold in March.

masser af.explanation: "Masser af" means "lots of". It is informal, and it works for things you can count and things you cannot: masser af mad (lots of food), masser af venner (lots of friends).

sentence.da: Vi har **masser af** mad.
sentence.en: We have lots of food.

matematik.explanation: "Matematik" means "math". Jeg er god til matematik means "I am good at math". The short form is matte.

sentence.da: I **matematik** lærer vi at regne med tal.
sentence.en: In math we learn to calculate with numbers.

mayonnaise.explanation: "Mayonnaise" means "mayonnaise", the thick white sauce. In everyday talk, Danes often shorten it to mayo.

sentence.da: Man laver **mayonnaise** af æg og olie.
sentence.en: You make mayonnaise from egg and oil.

med.explanation: "Med" means "with". Compare kaffe med mælk (coffee with milk) and kaffe uden mælk (coffee without milk). It is also used for coming or going along: Kom med! (Come along!), tage med (to go along).

forms.en: a cup of coffee with milk

sentence.da: Jeg drikker kaffe **med** mælk.
sentence.en: I drink coffee with milk.

med andre ord.explanation: "Med andre ord" means "in other words" and says the same thing again or sums it up: Bilen er gået i stykker. Med andre ord må vi tage toget (The car broke down. In other words, we must take the train).

sentence.da: Han er syg. **Med andre ord** kommer han ikke.
sentence.en: He is sick. In other words, he is not coming.

med det samme.explanation: "Med det samme" means "right away" or "immediately": Ring til mig med det samme (Call me right away). For something a little later, use om lidt (in a little while).

sentence.da: Jeg kommer **med det samme**.
sentence.en: I'm coming right away.

medicin.explanation: "En medicin" means "a medicine", something you take when you are ill: Jeg tager medicin hver dag (I take medicine every day).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og tager **medicin**.
sentence.en: I am sick and take medicine.

megen.explanation: "Megen" means "much" and is used with en-words you cannot count: megen tid (much time). It is mostly used in sentences with ikke (not) or with for (too): for megen støj (too much noise).

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke **megen** tid.
sentence.en: I do not have much time.

meget.explanation: "Meget" means "very" before a describing word: meget god (very good). With amounts it means "a lot" or "much": meget vand (a lot of water). For things you can count, use mange (many) instead.

forms.en: I have a lot of time.

sentence.da: Det er **meget** koldt i dag.
sentence.en: It is very cold today.

mel.explanation: "Mel" means "flour", the white powder you bake with. Do not mix it up with mælk (milk), which looks similar.

sentence.da: Jeg bager brød med **mel**.
sentence.en: I bake bread with flour.

mellem.explanation: "Mellem" means "between", for places, times and amounts: mellem to og tre (between two and three). It also works for a difference: forskellen mellem dem (the difference between them).

forms.en: between the house and the forest

sentence.da: Banken ligger **mellem** posthuset og skolen.
sentence.en: The bank is between the post office and the school.

mellemøsten.explanation: "Mellemøsten" means "the Middle East": Han er født i Mellemøsten (He was born in the Middle East). It is built from mellem (between) and øst (east).

forms.en: to travel to the Middle East
the war in the Middle East

sentence.da: Det er varmt og tørt i **Mellemøsten**.
sentence.en: It is hot and dry in the Middle East.

men.explanation: "Men" means "but". It joins two ideas that go against each other: Jeg er træt, men jeg kommer (I am tired, but I am coming). Do not mix it up with mens (while).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt, **men** glad.
sentence.en: I am tired, but happy.

menneskelig.explanation: "Menneskelig" means "human", about people: det menneskelige øje (the human eye). It can also mean kind and understanding: en menneskelig chef (a kind boss).

sentence.da: Det er en **menneskelig** fejl, ikke en computerfejl.
sentence.en: It is a human mistake, not a computer error.

mens.explanation: "Mens" means "while". It joins two things that happen at the same time: Hun synger, mens hun laver mad (She sings while she cooks). Do not mix it up with men (but).

sentence.da: Jeg læser, **mens** du sover.
sentence.en: I read while you sleep.

mere.explanation: "Mere" means "more" for amounts you cannot count: mere vand (more water). Before a describing word it makes a comparison: mere interessant (more interesting). Ikke mere means "no longer": Jeg bor ikke her mere (I don't live here anymore). For things you can count, use flere: flere biler (more cars).

sentence.da: Kan jeg få **mere** kaffe?
sentence.en: Can I have more coffee?

mest.explanation: "Mest" means "most" or "mostly". Before a describing word it means "the most": mest interessant (most interesting). With kan lide (like) it means "like best": Jeg kan mest lide kaffe (I like coffee best).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **mest** lide kaffe.
sentence.en: I like coffee the most.

mexicansk.explanation: "Mexicansk" means "Mexican" and describes things from Mexico: mexicansk mad (Mexican food). A person from Mexico is en mexicaner (a Mexican).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **mexicansk** mad hver fredag.
sentence.en: We eat Mexican food every Friday.

midnat.explanation: "Midnat" means "midnight", twelve o'clock at night: Vi går i seng efter midnat (We go to bed after midnight). Do not mix it up with middag, which means noon or dinner.

sentence.da: Festen slutter først ved **midnat**.
sentence.en: The party only ends at midnight.

midt.explanation: "Midt" means "in the middle". It usually comes with i (in) or på (on): midt i byen (in the middle of town), midt på dagen (in the middle of the day).

forms.en: in the middle of the room
in the middle of the night

sentence.da: Der står et træ **midt** i haven.
sentence.en: There is a tree in the middle of the garden.

mig.explanation: "Mig" means "me". Compare Jeg ser ham (I see him) with Han ser mig (He sees me). It also comes after little words: til mig (to me), med mig (with me). With some verbs it means "myself": Jeg vasker mig (I wash myself).

sentence.da: Min ven giver **mig** en gave.
sentence.en: My friend gives me a gift.

mild.explanation: "Mild" means "mild", gentle rather than strong: Osten smager mildt (The cheese tastes mild). It works for weather too: Vinteren er mild i år (The winter is mild this year).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have en **mild** sauce uden chili.
sentence.en: I want a mild sauce without chili.

million.explanation: "En million" means "a million". The thing you count comes after it: to millioner mennesker (two million people). Do not mix it up with en milliard, which means a billion (1,000 million).

sentence.da: Han vandt en **million** kroner i lotteriet.
sentence.en: He won a million kroner in the lottery.

min.explanation: "Min" means "my" or "mine" and is used with en-words: min bil (my car), min ven (my friend). For et-words, use mit (my), as in mit hus (my house), and for several things use mine, as in mine børn (my children).

sentence.da: Jeg har en bil. **Min** bil er rød.
sentence.en: I have a car. My car is red.

mindre.explanation: "Mindre" means both less (an amount) and smaller (a size): mindre kaffe (less coffee), et mindre hus (a smaller house).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker **mindre** kaffe nu.
sentence.en: I drink less coffee now.

mindst.explanation: "Mindst" means "least" and also "at least": Hvem har mindst tid? (Who has the least time?) With a number it sets the lowest amount: mindst fem (at least five).

forms.en: I will wait at least an hour

sentence.da: Du skal sove **mindst** otte timer.
sentence.en: You should sleep at least eight hours.

mine.explanation: "Mine" means "my" or "mine" when there is more than one thing. Compare min bog (my book) with mine bøger (my books), and mit hus (my house) with mine huse (my houses). It also works alone: Bøgerne er mine (The books are mine).

sentence.da: **Mine** børn hedder Peter og Anna.
sentence.en: My children are called Peter and Anna.

minigolf.explanation: "Minigolf" means "mini golf", the small golf game with fun obstacles: Minigolf er sjovt (Mini golf is fun).

sentence.da: Vi skal spille **minigolf**, når solen skinner.
sentence.en: We are going to play mini golf when the sun shines.

misundelig.explanation: "Misundelig" means "envious", wanting what someone else has. Add på (of) and the person: Han er misundelig på sin kollega (He is envious of his coworker).

sentence.da: Jeg er **misundelig** på din nye bil.
sentence.en: I am envious of your new car.

mit.explanation: "Mit" means "my" or "mine" for words that go with et. Compare mit hus (my house, because et hus) with min bil (my car, because en bil), and mine huse (my houses, more than one). It also works alone: Huset er mit (The house is mine).

sentence.da: Jeg har et hus. **Mit** hus er gult.
sentence.en: I have a house. My house is yellow.

mod.explanation: "Mod" means "toward" and also "against". Compare Han går mod døren (He walks toward the door) with Vi spiller mod Sverige (We play against Sweden). To say you are against an idea, use imod: Jeg er imod det (I am against it).

sentence.da: Vi går **mod** stationen.
sentence.en: We are walking toward the station.

mode.explanation: "Mode" means "fashion", the clothes and styles people like now: Hun elsker mode (She loves fashion). Don't confuse it with måde (way), as in en god måde (a good way).

sentence.da: Min søster elsker **mode** og køber meget tøj.
sentence.en: My sister loves fashion and buys a lot of clothes.

moderne.explanation: "Moderne" means "modern": Huset er meget moderne (The house is very modern). It also fits styles and art: moderne kunst (modern art). The opposite is gammeldags (old-fashioned).

sentence.da: Vi bor i et **moderne** hus med store vinduer.
sentence.en: We live in a modern house with big windows.

modig.explanation: "Modig" means "brave" and describes someone who dares to do hard or scary things: Han var modig og sagde nej (He was brave and said no). The opposite is bange (scared).

sentence.da: Hun er **modig** og tør tale foran hundrede mennesker.
sentence.en: She is brave and dares to speak in front of a hundred people.

modsat.explanation: "Modsat" means "opposite", the other way around: Før er det modsatte af efter (Before is the opposite of after). Han bor på den modsatte side af gaden (He lives on the opposite side of the street).

sentence.da: Han gik til højre, og jeg gik i **modsat** retning.
sentence.en: He went right, and I went in the opposite direction.

moms.explanation: "Moms" means "VAT" or "sales tax", the tax that is added to prices in shops: Er det med moms? (Is VAT included?) Prisen med moms er højere (The price with VAT is higher).

sentence.da: Prisen er tusind kroner med **moms**.
sentence.en: The price is a thousand kroner with VAT.

morgenmad.explanation: "Morgenmad" means "breakfast". It is morgen (morning) and mad (food) joined together. No a is needed: Jeg spiser morgenmad (I eat breakfast).

sentence.da: Om morgenen spiser jeg **morgenmad**: brød og kaffe.
sentence.en: In the morning I eat breakfast: bread and coffee.

morsom.explanation: "Morsom" means "funny" in a light, amusing way: Han er en morsom fyr (He is an amusing guy). In everyday speech, many people say sjov (fun) instead.

sentence.da: Han fortalte en **morsom** historie.
sentence.en: He told a funny story.

motion.explanation: "Motion" means "exercise", physical activity that is good for you: Jeg dyrker motion tre gange om ugen (I exercise three times a week). Du får ikke nok motion (You do not get enough exercise).

sentence.da: Jeg går en lang tur for at få **motion**.
sentence.en: I take a long walk to get exercise.

motivation.explanation: "Motivation" means "motivation", the drive to do something: Jeg har ingen motivation i dag (I have no motivation today). Gode mål giver motivation (Good goals give motivation).

sentence.da: Jeg har ingen **motivation** til at træne.
sentence.en: I have no motivation to exercise.

mozzarella.explanation: "Mozzarella" means "mozzarella", a soft, mild Italian cheese that melts well: Jeg bruger mozzarella på pizzaen (I use mozzarella on the pizza).

sentence.da: Til salaten køber jeg frisk **mozzarella** og tomater.
sentence.en: For the salad, I buy fresh mozzarella and tomatoes.

mulig.explanation: "Mulig" means "possible": Det er muligt (It is possible). It is also in a useful set phrase: så hurtigt som muligt (as fast as possible).

sentence.da: Er der en **mulig** løsning?
sentence.en: Is there a possible solution?

muligvis.explanation: "Muligvis" means "possibly" and is built from mulig (possible): Hun er muligvis syg (She is possibly sick). It can also answer a question: Kommer hun? Muligvis. (Is she coming? Possibly.)

sentence.da: Vi tager **muligvis** til Spanien i sommer.
sentence.en: We are possibly going to Spain this summer.

musik.explanation: "Musik" means "music". It is used without en or "et": Jeg elsker musik (I love music). For a school lesson, Jeg har musik means "I have music class".

sentence.da: Jeg lytter gerne til **musik**.
sentence.en: I like listening to music.

musikalsk.explanation: "Musikalsk" means "musical", like having a talent for music: Hun er meget musikalsk (She is very musical). It also describes things: en musikalsk familie (a musical family).

sentence.da: Min datter er meget **musikalsk** og elsker at synge.
sentence.en: My daughter is very musical and loves to sing.

mystisk.explanation: "Mystisk" means "mysterious", strange and hard to explain: Det hele virker mystisk (It all seems mysterious). Det var en mystisk historie (It was a mysterious story).

sentence.da: Der står en **mystisk** mand uden for vores dør.
sentence.en: A mysterious man is standing outside our door.

må jeg bede om regningen?.explanation: "Må jeg bede om regningen?" means "May I have the bill?" and is a polite way to ask for it at a restaurant. Må jeg bede om means "may I ask for". A shorter everyday way is Regningen, tak (The bill, please).

sentence.da: Vi har spist. **Må jeg bede om regningen?**
sentence.en: We have eaten. May I have the bill?

må jeg få regningen?.explanation: "Må jeg få regningen?" means "May I have the bill?" Må jeg få works for anything you ask for politely: Må jeg få en kop kaffe? (May I have a cup of coffee?). Adding tak (please, thanks) at the end sounds friendly.

forms.da: Må jeg få en kop kaffe?
forms.en: May I have a cup of coffee?

related.en: May I have the bill? (more formal)

sentence.da: Maden var god. **Må jeg få regningen?**
sentence.en: The food was good. May I have the bill?

måske.explanation: "Måske" means "maybe" or "perhaps". Compare Kommer du? Ja! (Are you coming? Yes!) with Kommer du? Måske. (Are you coming? Maybe). It can also start a sentence: Måske regner det i morgen (Maybe it will rain tomorrow).

sentence.da: **Måske** kommer han i morgen.
sentence.en: Maybe he will come tomorrow.

mælk.explanation: "Mælk" means "milk": Jeg drikker mælk (I drink milk). To count it, use a measure: en liter mælk (a liter of milk).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker et glas **mælk** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I drink a glass of milk every morning.

mærkelig.explanation: "Mærkelig" means "strange" and is used for something odd that you notice: Det er mærkeligt (That is strange). Det lød mærkeligt (It sounded strange).

sentence.da: Der er en **mærkelig** lyd i køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a strange sound in the kitchen.

mæt.explanation: "Mæt" means "full" after eating: Jeg er mæt (I am full) is a polite way to turn down more food. Do not use fuld after a meal: Jeg er fuld means "I am drunk".

sentence.da: Jeg har spist meget og er **mæt**.
sentence.en: I have eaten a lot and am full.

møbleret.explanation: "Møbleret" means "furnished", for a room or apartment that comes with furniture: Lejligheden er møbleret (The apartment is furnished). Without furniture, say umøbleret (unfurnished).

sentence.da: Jeg leder efter et **møbleret** værelse.
sentence.en: I am looking for a furnished room.

mør.explanation: "Mør" means "tender", for meat that is soft and easy to cut: Kødet er mør (The meat is tender). The opposite is sej (tough): Kødet er sejt (The meat is tough).

sentence.da: Kødet er **mør** og smager dejligt.
sentence.en: The meat is tender and tastes lovely.

mørk.explanation: "Mørk" means "dark": i mørket (in the dark). It also goes in front of colors: mørkeblå (dark blue).

sentence.da: Natten er meget **mørk**.
sentence.en: The night is very dark.

mørke.explanation: "Mørke" means "darkness": Mørket falder på tidligt om vinteren (Darkness falls early in the winter). To describe something dark, use mørk: et mørkt rum (a dark room).

sentence.da: Vi sidder i **mørke**, når strømmen går.
sentence.en: We sit in the dark when the power goes out.

mørkeblå.explanation: "Mørkeblå" means "dark blue" or "navy". It is built from mørk (dark) and blå (blue).

sentence.da: Min jakke er **mørkeblå**.
sentence.en: My jacket is dark blue.

mørkegrøn.explanation: "Mørkegrøn" means "dark green". It is built from mørk (dark) and grøn (green).

sentence.da: Min bil er **mørkegrøn**.
sentence.en: My car is dark green.

müsli.explanation: "Müsli" means "muesli", the breakfast mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit. It is used without en or "et": Jeg spiser müsli (I eat muesli).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **müsli** med mælk i en skål.
sentence.en: I eat muesli with milk in a bowl.
